$comment: Activity-detection patterns, read from here rather than compiled in.
An agent's wording is not ours to control: Claude, Codex and the rest
reword their prompts whenever they like, and a changed phrase used to mean
the app no longer noticed that agent waiting for an answer — fixable only
by a new release. This file ships inside the binary as a fallback, and the
app refreshes it from the repository in the background, so a wording change
can be fixed by editing this file alone.
waiting: lowercase substrings matched against the pane's last lines. Keep
them distinctive: a phrase that also appears in ordinary output makes the
spinners: characters an agent animates while it works. Presence of one is
the primary busy signal, so a character the agent prints for other reasons
would make it look permanently busy.
version: increment when changing anything here. The app only replaces its
copy with a higher version, so an older file cannot overwrite a newer one.
$comment_backgroundAgentBusy: Case-insensitive regular expressions, matched against the whole pane, meaning a spawned agent is still working while the main thread sits idle. Only Claude Code's explicit sentence qualifies. The status bar's "← 1 agent" was tried and removed: that count is how many agents the session HAS, not how many are running, so it stays on screen after the work finishes and marked finished sessions busy.
backgroundAgentBusy: waiting for \d+ background agents? to finish

antigravity.$comment: Measured off a running agy 1.2.3, not copied from Gemini: the harness is a rewrite and words its prompts its own way. Two prompts were seen — the permission dialog ("Requesting permission for:" / "Run this command?" over a numbered list ending in "No, cancel") and the trust prompt a fresh workspace shows before the agent has done anything. "esc to cancel" is deliberately absent: it sits in the footer throughout a turn, including under the permission dialog, so it means busy rather than waiting. The extra spinners are the denser half of the braille block, none of which is in the default set.

codex.$comment: Codex phrases its approval prompt its own way; the generic wording never appears, so those alone left every Codex question undetected.
waiting: tell codex what to do differently

cursor.$comment: Taken from a captured approval prompt, not from the documentation. The generic wording that was here first ("allow once", "(y/n)") matched a Go source listing in the transcript and held a session on "waiting". "Run Everything" is deliberately absent although it is one of the answers offered: it is also the footer's standing mode label, on screen while the agent is idle. Busy is read from "ctrl+c to stop" in the footer, which needs no pattern here.
